text:
Priya (PM): heads up — competitorX just announced per-route cost routing + instant model fallback. saw it in their partner newsletter. we should evaluate impact on our roadmap.
Alex (Eng): saw that. looks like an optimization layer + policy UI. not core infra but could influence Dedicated/Private asks.
Marta (PMM): copy. customers will expect a story about cost controls and predictable fallbacks. we need a comms plan if we don't have parity.
Jamie (Eng-Platform): quick reality check: we already have fallback routing by model family. per-route cost policies would need routing + cost-estimator + UI. rough estimate 4 sprint effort to ship a safe MVP with basic rules.
Priya (PM): OK — can we do a spike to see if we can reuse current smart routing? Alex, Jamie — can you own a 1-week spike? goal: prove out per-route policy config + fallback hooks.
Alex (Eng): I can take the spike. will mock a policy layer and reuse existing fallback code. deliverable: prototype + perf notes.
Ryan (Sales): FYI a couple enterprise customers asked for finer cost controls yesterday. timing could help renewals.
Sam (Design): if engineering can surface policies as simple toggles + overrides we can copy into marketing and docs quickly.
Marta (PMM): let's avoid parity for parity's sake — we should map which bits customers actually care about (cost routing vs instant fallback vs UI). can we get customer signals in 48h?
Priya (PM): Ryan — can you pull notes from yesterday's calls and flag customers who would push for this? prioritize ones with Dedicated/contracts.
Ryan (Sales): on it. will post list in #customer-success by EOD.
Alex (Eng): spike plan: 3 tasks — 1) policy proto (yaml-based rules), 2) hook into router for cost estimation, 3) smoke test fallback flows. will update by tomorrow noon.
Jamie (Eng-Platform): also need infra cost estimate. quick back-of-envelope: MVP may need ~2 additional autoscale rules + one feature flag.
Priya (PM): Good. Tentative decision: run spike, collect customer signals, then sync on scope tradeoff. If spike is positive, propose a 3-sprint scoped initiative: parity-lite (routing + fallback + metrics) with deferred full UI.
Marta (PMM): messaging for external: emphasize our existing routing strengths (multi-tier fallbacks, KV caching) and show roadmap step: "cost-policy primitives" in beta. avoids claiming full parity while setting expectation.
Sam (Design): will draft a beta banner and a short UX flow for toggles.
Alex (Eng): quick note — fallback semantics: prefer lower-cost compatible model, then region fallback. need to document compatibility rules.
Priya (PM): action items: Alex/Jamie spike (1wk), Ryan customer list (EOD), Sam design draft (2 days), Marta draft comms (2 days). follow-up sync Friday 10am PST.
deploy-bot: scheduled meeting created for Fri 10:00 PST — Priya, Alex, Jamie, Marta, Ryan, Sam
Ryan (Sales): +1. if legal/customer requires contract addendum we'll escalate.
Marta (PMM): also tracking KPIs: % requests routed to fallback, avg token-cost delta, and customer satisfaction signal.
Priya (PM): agreed. if spike shows >20% complexity vs value we'll push to backlog and craft a public roadmap note.
Alex (Eng): starting spike now. will paste prototype snippets here.
Alex (Eng): ```yaml
policy:
  - route: /gen-image
    prefer: cost
    thresholds:
      max_latency_ms: 250
      max_token_cost: 0.002
    fallbacks:
      - model: small-compat-v2
      - region: us-west-2
```
Priya (PM): thanks. this is the right level for a prototype.
Sam (Design): small nit — in the UI we should call it "cost policy" not "prefer: cost". customers find plain language easier.
Alex (Eng): noted. will update proto.
Priya (PM): great thread. we'll reconvene Fri after spike. thanks all. :thumbsup:
